song_story.overview: One of DAY6's signature songs, built almost entirely around a single repeated word: 예뻤어 — 'you were beautiful,' past tense. The singer is clear upfront that he's not trying to get back together — he's just been hit by a memory and wants to say it out loud once. What follows is a list of small, specific things he misses: the way she looked at him, the sound of her voice saying his name, being told good morning and good night without fail. It's a breakup song about gratitude more than grief — accepting that something is over while still honoring that it was good.
song_story.cultural_root: The whole song hinges on the difference between 예뻐 (present tense, 'you are beautiful') and 예뻤어 (past tense, 'you were beautiful') — a distinction English doesn't mark as sharply. Saying it in the past tense is the entire emotional argument: he's not calling her beautiful now, he's certifying that she was, back then, and that this fact doesn't change just because the relationship ended.

verse_1.lines: 지금 이 말이jigeum i mari / 우리가 다시uriga dasi / 시작하자는 건 아냐sijakajaneun geon anya / 그저 너의geujeo neoui / 남아있던 기억들이namaitdeon gieokdeuri / 떠올랐을 뿐이야tteoollasseul ppuniya / 정말 하루도 빠짐없이 (너는)jeongmal harudo ppajimeopsi (neoneun) / 사랑한다 말해줬었지saranghanda malhaejwosseotji / 잠들기 전에 또 눈 뜨자마자jamdeulgi jeone tto nun tteujamaja / 말해주던 너malhaejudeon neo / 생각이 나 말해보는 거야saenggagi na malhaeboneun geoya / 예뻤어yeppeosseo / 날 바라봐 주던 그 눈빛nal barabwa judeon geu nunbit / 날 불러주던 그 목소리nal bulleojudeon geu moksori / 다 다da da
verse_1.literal: What I'm saying right now / isn't that we should start over again / it's just that / some memory of you that had been staying inside me / suddenly floated up
verse_1.context: 다시 시작하자는 건 아냐 — 'this isn't [me] saying let's start again' — the song opens by explicitly ruling out reconciliation, which is unusual; most breakup songs either want the person back or are still processing anger. This one starts from acceptance.

verse_1_close.lines: 그 모든 게 내겐geu modeun ge naegen / 예뻤어yeppeosseo / 더 바랄게 없는듯한 느낌deo baralge eomneundeutan neukkim / 오직 너만이 주던 순간들ojik neomani judeon sun-gandeul / 다 다da da / 지났지만jinatjiman / 넌 너무 예뻤어neon neomu yeppeosseo / 너도 이제는 (이제)neodo ijeneun (ije) / 나와의 기억이nawaui gieogi / 추억이 되었을 거야chueogi doe-eosseul geoya / 너에게는neoegeneun / 어떤 말을 해도 다eotteon mareul haedo da / 지나간 일일 거야jinagan iril geoya / 정말 한번도 빠짐없이 (너는)jeongmal hanbeondo ppajimeopsi (neoneun) / 나를 먼저 생각해줬어nareul meonjeo saenggakaejwosseo
verse_1_close.literal: Really, without missing a single day, you / used to tell me you loved me / right before falling asleep and right after opening your eyes / you, who used to say it / I'm thinking of it, so I'm trying to say it out loud
verse_1_close.context: 빠짐없이 (without exception/missing anything) emphasizes consistency — this wasn't a one-time gesture, it was daily ritual, which is exactly the kind of thing that becomes unbearably noticeable once it's gone.

chorus.lines: 아무 일 아니어도 미안해 고마워amu il anieodo mianhae gomawo / 해주던 너haejudeon neo / 생각이 나 말해보는 거야saenggagi na malhaeboneun geoya / 예뻤어yeppeosseo / 날 바라봐 주던 그 눈빛nal barabwa judeon geu nunbit / 날 불러주던 그 목소리nal bulleojudeon geu moksori / 다 다da da / 그 모든 게 내겐geu modeun ge naegen / 예뻤어yeppeosseo / 더 바랄게 없는듯한 느낌deo baralge eomneundeutan neukkim / 오직 너만이 주던 순간들ojik neomani judeon sun-gandeul / 다 다da da / 지났지만jinatjiman / 넌 너무 예뻤어neon neomu yeppeosseo / 아직도 가끔 네 생각이 나ajikdo gakkeum ne saenggagi na
chorus.literal: You were beautiful / the way you used to look at me, that gaze / the voice that used to call my name / all of it, all of it / all of that, to me
chorus.context: 예뻤어 stands alone as its own line — a complete sentence, past tense, no object needed. Repeating 다 다 (all, all) at the end of each chorus line drives home that it's not one specific memory being praised, it's the entirety of the relationship.

bridge.lines: 어렵게 전화를 걸어볼까eoryeopge jeonhwareul georeobolkka / 생각이 들 때도 많지만saenggagi deul ttaedo manjiman / 아무리 원해도 너는 이제amuri wonhaedo neoneun ije / 이미 끝나버린 지난날의imi kkeunnabeorin jinannarui / 한편의 영화였었단 걸hanpyeonui yeonghwayeosseotdan geol / 난 알아nan ara / 마지막majimak / 날 바라봐 주던 그 눈빛nal barabwa judeon geu nunbit / 잘 지내라던 그 목소리jal jinaeradeon geu moksori / 다 다da da / 그마저도 내겐geumajeodo naegen / 예뻤어yeppeosseo / 내게 보여준 눈물까지naege boyeojun nunmulkkaji / 너와 가졌던 순간들은neowa gajyeotdeon sun-gandeureun / 다 다da da / 지났지만jinatjiman / 넌 너무 예뻤어neon neomu yeppeosseo
bridge.literal: Even now, sometimes I still think of you / should I try calling, even though it's hard? / thoughts like that come to me often too, but / baby, I know it's already over
bridge.context: This is the moment the accepting mask slips slightly — he admits he still thinks about calling. -지만 (but/although) pivots straight back to acceptance: 이미 끝나버린 걸 난 알아, 'I know it's already ended.' The honesty about temptation makes the acceptance feel earned rather than performed.

artist_context: You Were Beautiful is one of DAY6's most enduring hits, frequently cited by fans as a defining song for the band and a staple of their live performances, where its full-band arrangement lets the chorus build into something much bigger than a typical ballad.
honorific_level: informal — 반말, spoken as a private, almost accidental confession rather than a message meant to reach her

grammar_highlights.usage: Korean adjectives conjugate for tense just like verbs. 예뻤어 (was beautiful) vs 예뻐 (is beautiful) — the entire song's meaning depends on this single tense shift.
'It's not that ___.' 시작하자는 건 아냐 = 'it's not that [I'm saying] let's start over' — used to preemptively clarify intent and avoid misunderstanding.
'Without exception, without missing any.' 하루도 빠짐없이 = 'without missing a single day' — emphasizes total consistency, making its loss feel larger.
